decisions.unsure: A small upright x is printed high at the end of the group, standing free above a plain caret-shaped D54; it touches no other sign and there is no viper in the word, so it cannot be I9's horns.
decisions.why: The x is printed in the hieroglyph line, the same size and weight as Budge's Z9 elsewhere (T'afi), and is set apart from the legs. Coded as the crossed-sticks sign Z9, stacked over D54. It may be Budge copying a mark in the papyrus rather than a word-sign; the note keeps that open.

decisions.unsure: The tether lies flat with two loops at the left end and the small walking legs joined under its middle: the single sign V15 (tether + legs).
decisions.why: House rulings (Spell 17 part 2: 'θet has D54'; parts 4-5: 'θet V13 + D54'; established ani-017-b) code this same ligature as V13 + D54, so A, and V13 is marked approx. V15 is the exact Gardiner sign; established hymn-to-osiris has V15, so the house is not consistent here — if the lead prefers V15, B is right for all three.

decisions.unsure: The middle sign is a closed parallelogram: slanted left end, closed square right end. It is the same shape as the plinth in maāχeru on pp. 97–98. The em sign on p. 99 (Aa15) has an open right end.
decisions.why: Code what is printed. House rule: closed plinth Aa11, open bevelled sign Aa15. The sign is closed, so Aa11 (approx). By sense this is setem's m (Aa15), so the type has used the plinth for it.

decisions.unsure: The sickle U1 is drawn as a double-lined curved blade with a small separate bar at its upper left. That bar is the sickle's handle as this type draws U1, not a plinth: it is short and round-ended, unlike the long slanted Aa11 of this type. Under it is a flat arm with an upright hand (D36).
decisions.why: This is U1 + D36 + P8, as in the Spell 17 part 3 ruling 'maā U1 D36 where so printed'. There is no separate Aa11.

decisions.unsure: The owl is drawn obliquely: a long diagonal body with the ear-tufted head at the upper left, a small arch for the feet below. The flat arm D36, with its tab at the right, runs across it. This is the owl-arm ligature, not a sickle: the U1 sickle on p. 99 is a crescent with a handle.
decisions.why: House ruling: the owl-over-arm ligature read mā is G17 + D36 (established 125-address, 017). Budge reads mā.

decisions.unsure: A horizontal bolt with small walking legs joined under its middle: one ligature.
decisions.why: This is the Gardiner sign O35 (bolt + legs). The established sebi in 125-address is also O35.

decisions.unsure: After X1 over N35: a tall upright with a hooked top and an H-like crossbar, and set close beside it a bird with raised wings and its body slanting down (G41-like), not standing on the upright. Then Y1a.
decisions.why: Two signs, not a heron on a perch (B's G32): the bird stands beside the post, not on top of it. The house coded the same pair in tennu (ani-018-a) as a forked pole O30 approx + G41 approx, so use that rather than A's Aa28.

decisions.unsure: Budge prints 'ḥràu' with an accented à. The face sits over a short stroke, then a dashed stroke and a seated god.
decisions.why: B's transliteration matches the print. Signs are the same in both; B's q shows D2 stacked over Z1.

decisions.unsure: Second sign: a wider box over a narrower box, with a small loop on a stem on top. The determinative after N29 is an oval open at the left with finger-like lines inside, like a closed fist with its wrist stub.
decisions.why: The second sign must read sꜣ. V33 (A) is not a sꜣ sign. V17 (B) is a rolled shelter, not stacked boxes. The established saqa (ani-147-b) uses Aa18 approx. For the determinative, A's fist D49 approx fits the shape better than B's V33 bag; D49 is kept approx.

decisions.unsure: After the bird: a short bold stroke raised at the top of the line, then a full-height dashed stroke. No footnote on p. 103 to go with the short stroke.
decisions.why: Without a footnote, the raised short stroke is a stroke, not a footnote mark. The established baiu in ani-017-a and ani-018-b codes R7 G29 Z1 Z1. B.

decisions.unsure: The owl is drawn obliquely: a long diagonal body with the ear-tufted head at the upper left, a small arch for the feet below. The flat arm D36, with its tab at the right, runs across it. This is the owl-arm ligature, not a sickle: the U1 sickle on p. 99 is a crescent with a handle. The rest matches both readers.
decisions.why: Same ligature as in mā; established māχent is G17 D36 F32 …

decisions.unsure: Under the bolt: a horizontal sign whose left end turns down and whose right end hangs in a small loop. Then X1, two tall upright strokes with slanted tops, and Y1a.
decisions.why: This is the hooked phallus-with-issue D53 of met, which the house codes D53 (embaḥ, met, meter; established semetert in 125-address: O34 D53 X1 …). Neither V12 nor F21 fits. Strokes Z4A, as B, per the ruling 'two upright strokes Z4A'.

decisions.unsure: Two tall upright strokes with slanted tops after the vulture, the same as in semet.
decisions.why: House ruling: two upright strokes are Z4A; Z4 is for oblique strokes.

decisions.unsure: At high zoom the small kneeling figure has its arm brought up to the face (hand to mouth).
decisions.why: House ruling: A2 in ren where printed hand to mouth.

decisions.unsure: The oar is a long oblique shaft with a small cross-piece at the top and a spoon blade at the lower right. The horizontal curved stick after it is M3.
decisions.why: The cross-piece at the top marks a steering oar (P10), which is the right determinative for ḥemi 'rudder'. The plain oar P8 of maāχeru has no cross-piece.

decisions.unsure: Under the first group Budge prints 'màtet' with a grave accent on the a.
decisions.why: Signs are the same in both readers (W19, X1 X1 over Y1). B's transliteration matches the print.

decisions.unsure: At the upper right a small tilted wedge, tapering to a point at the upper left and rounded at the lower right, over a stroke.
decisions.why: House ruling: a small wedge is N21 (approx) where land is meant. M44 (thorn) is not used for this shape in the house rulings.

decisions.unsure: A small oval pot with a cap on top and short rays (lugs) on each side.
decisions.why: The established ḥeq (ani-001-b, ani-022-072) codes this same lugged oval pot as W22 approx. Kept consistent with that.

decisions.unsure: The first sign is an open rectangle with a gap in the middle of its bottom line: the house sign O1. The p-stool Q3 in this type (pen, on the same page) is a closed square. Long rounded loaf with an oblique double line (X4 approx).
decisions.why: Code what is printed: O1, although Budge reads p. Flag for the lead as a probable type confusion.

decisions.unsure: First sign: a flat hand, rounded fingers at the left, thumb bump on top, flared wrist at the right (D46). Determinative: the same lugged pot as in māḥerà. Budge prints '(sic)' after ṭeni in the transliteration line.
decisions.why: D46 fits the shape and Budge's ṭ. The pot is W22 approx as in māḥerà and the established ḥeq. The established convention keeps '(sic)' in budge.

decisions.unsure: A seated figure with a human-style seated body and knee, and a jackal head with ears and snout.
decisions.why: This is a jackal-headed god (C6), not a crouching jackal (E15/E16). Established Ànpu has C6.

decisions.unsure: The tree M1 has a curved stick laid across its crown. The stick turns down at the left and has an arrow-like tip at the right: the same horizontal branch M3 as after ḥemi.
decisions.why: The branch is a separate sign set over the tree, so code it.

decisions.unsure: The face D2 stands on a short vertical stem that joins the heart jar's rim. The stem is a separate stroke: the jar's own rim has its lugs below it, and the F34 jars on p. 98 have no such stem.
decisions.why: House rulings: ḥer-àb is D2 Z1 F34 where the stroke is printed (Spell 17 part 3, established 017-c, 018-introduction).

decisions.unsure: Under D21: a flat hand with rounded fingers at the left, thumb bump on top and wrist at the right, the same sign as in ṭeni and t'eṭet. Then the loop with a crossing stick (T12 approx).
decisions.why: D46 matches Budge's ṭ and the established ruṭ (125-address, 023-024: D21 D46 T12).

decisions.unsure: Under D21: a flat hand with rounded fingers at the left, thumb bump on top and wrist at the right, the same sign as in ṭeni and t'eṭet. Then the loop with a crossing stick (T12 approx). Figure with hand to mouth (A2).
decisions.why: Same as ruṭ - s.
